  "text": "The constable took a step toward the stairs. Ada held out her arm.

“She’s dead,” she said.

Below them, the front-door latch clicked. The constable looked down at the key still hanging from his belt.

Venn folded the yellow paper along its old creases. “The warning said not to answer until it asks to leave. Did the voice ask?”

Ada thought of the sigh behind the door. She remembered. Not a question. Not even a request.

The six letters on the floor began to turn, each one scraping a slow circle in the dust. From downstairs came the sound of wet shoes crossing the hall.

“Mara,” Ada called, “what was carved beneath your name?”

The footsteps stopped.

For a moment there was only rain, pattering impossibly through the open brass gate. Then Mara’s voice rose from the landing below. “You know what it says.”

“I know what I read.” Ada glanced at the letters. They had come to rest in a different order. “I’m asking you.”

The lantern guttered. In its wavering light, Ada saw water creeping up the stairs, step by step, though nothing spilled over the edges.

Venn crouched beside the letters. “This isn’t her name,” he whispered.

At the bottom of the stairs, Mara laughed once. It sounded like a woman recognizing a familiar mistake.

Ada picked up the first letter. The water halted.

“Tell me whose name it is,” she said.

The brass gate snapped shut. Every scratch returned to the door at once, deep enough to show pale wood beneath the paint. Downstairs, the wet footsteps began to climb."
